necessary_context.content: g(x)=(1/n) sum_i f_i(x), x in R^p. Each f_i is convex and differentiable with globally L-Lipschitz gradient in Euclidean norm; a minimizer x* exists. Data/functions are fixed.
necessary_context.locator: Eq.(1), p.2; Section 3, p.7; Appendix B.1, pp.34–35
necessary_context.name: Finite-sum model

necessary_context.content: At each update select a fresh uniform component index; expectations concern these indices. Appendix B.1 uses k>=1, refresh at x^(k-1), then form x^k. This is the indexing used in this batch; Section 1 Eq.(5)–(6) uses a shifted presentation. Zero table initialization is y_i^0=0.
necessary_context.locator: Eq.(5)–(6), p.3; Section 3, p.7; Algorithm 1, p.10; Appendix B.1, p.35
necessary_context.name: Randomness, initialization and indexing

necessary_context.content: bar x^k=(1/k) sum_{t=0}^{k-1} x^t; sigma^2=(1/n) sum_i ||grad f_i(x*)||^2. Strong convexity means g(x)-(mu/2)||x||^2 is convex, mu>0. Theorem 1 also treats a centered-gradient initialization, outside the selected targets' scope.
